Multivariate Analysis Coursework

Supporting R work

Overview

This document presents the R workflow that supports the accompanying multivariate analysis report. It is intentionally sparse, the report contains the detailed interpretation, while this page focuses on the data preparation, visualisations and statistical calculations.

Data preparation

The required packages are loaded, the athletics data are imported and the 800 m results are converted from minutes to seconds. The four event variables are then collected in a matrix for analysis.

library(gridExtra)
library(ggplot2)

data = read.table('athlrecs.txt')
data["m800"] = data["m800"] * 60 # convert minutes to seconds
X = as.matrix(data[,1:4])

knitr::kable(
  summary(X),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Summary statistics for race times (seconds)",
  align = "c"
)

Exploratory analysis

Event distributions and scaled summaries

The following calculations compare the centre and spread of event times after scaling each distance to an 800 m equivalent. The boxplots provide a visual summary of each event distribution.

X_IQR = apply(X, 2, IQR)

average_X_scaled = colMeans(X) * c(8,4,2,1)
X_IQR_scaled = X_IQR * c(8,4,2,1)

scaled_results = rbind(
  "Scaled Mean" = average_X_scaled,
  "Scaled IQR" = X_IQR_scaled
)

knitr::kable(
  scaled_results,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Scaled summary statistics by event",
  align = "c"
)
Scaled summary statistics by event
m100 m200 m400 m800
Scaled Mean 83.769 83.761 92.877 107.596
Scaled IQR 2.560 2.760 3.480 3.600 
par(mfrow = c(1,4))
colours = c("turquoise", "pink", "mediumpurple1", "lightsteelblue1")
for (i in seq_along(colnames(X))){
  col = colnames(X)[i]
  boxplot(X[,col],
          main = paste("Distribution of", col),
          ylab = "Time (seconds)",
          col = colours[i])
}

Pairwise relationships

Pairwise scatterplots and 95% normal ellipses are used as an assessment of the relationships between event times.

mean_vect = colMeans(X)
n_cols = length(colnames(X))
plots = list()
for (i in seq_len(n_cols - 1)) {
  for (j in seq((i + 1), n_cols)) {
    col1 = colnames(X)[i]
    col2 = colnames(X)[j]
    p = ggplot(X, aes_string(col1, col2)) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.7, colour = "mediumpurple1") +
      labs(title = paste(col1, "vs", col2),
           x = col1,
           y = col2) +
      stat_ellipse(type = "norm",
                   level = 0.95,
                   color = "lightsteelblue1",
                   size = 1) +
      theme_minimal()
    plots[[length(plots) + 1]] = p
  }
}
do.call(grid.arrange, c(plots, ncol = 3))

Proportionality of race times

This section implements the one-sample Hotelling’s \(T^2\) test to see whether mean race time scales proportionally with event distance.

One-sample Hotelling’s test

A = matrix(c(0,0,-2,1,
             0,-4,2,0,
             -8,4,0,0), nrow = 3, byrow = T)
Y = X%*%t(A)


y_bar = colMeans(Y)
mu_0 = c(0,0,0)
S = var(Y)
n = dim(Y)[1]
m = n-1
p = dim(Y)[2]
tsq = n * t(y_bar) %*% solve(S) %*% y_bar
fstat = (n-p)/(p*m) * tsq

df1 = p
df2 = n-p

p_val = pf(fstat, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, lower.tail = F)
One-sample Hotelling’s T-squared test
Result Value
Hotelling’s T-squared (tsq) 5858.7473
F statistic (fstat) 1880.5855
Numerator degrees of freedom (df1) 3
Denominator degrees of freedom (df2) 52
p-value (p_val) 5.494e-53

Simultaneous confidence intervals

compute_CI = function(a, y_bar, S, p, n, df1, df2) {
  critical_val = sqrt(((p * (n-1)) / (n-p)) * qf(0.95, df1, df2) * (1 / n))
  margin = critical_val * sqrt(t(a) %*% S %*% a)
  c(t(a) %*% y_bar - margin, t(a) %*% y_bar + margin)
}

a_vectors = diag(p)
CIs = apply(a_vectors, 2, compute_CI, y_bar, S, p, n, df1, df2)

Comparison by country status

The final analysis compares the multivariate event-time profiles of the two country-status groups used in the source data.

Group distributions and two-sample Hotelling’s test

X2 = as.matrix(cbind(X, data["status"]))

par(mfrow = c(2,2))
for (col in colnames(X2[,1:4])){
  boxplot(X2[,col] ~ X2[,"status"],
          main = col,
          xlab = "Country Status",
          ylab = "Time (s)",
          col = c("mediumpurple1", "lightsteelblue1"))
}

X1 = X2[X2[, "status"] == 1, ]
X2 = X2[X2[, "status"] == 3, ]
X1 = X1[, colnames(X2) != "status"]
X2 = X2[, colnames(X2) != "status"]


x_1bar = colMeans(X1)
x_2bar = colMeans(X2)
p = dim(X1)[2]

S_1 = cov(X1)
S_2 = cov(X2)

n_1 = dim(X1)[1]
n_2 = dim(X2)[1]


S = ((n_1 - 1)*S_1 + (n_2 - 1)*S_2)/(n_1 + n_2 - 2)

tsq = (n_1*n_2)/(n_1 + n_2) *
  t(x_1bar - x_2bar) %*% solve(S) %*% (x_1bar - x_2bar)
df1 = p
df2 = n_1 + n_2 - p - 1

fstat = (n_1 + n_2 - p - 1)/((n_1 + n_2 - 2)*p) * tsq

p_val = pf(fstat, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, lower.tail = F)
Two-sample Hotelling’s T-squared test
Result Value
Hotelling’s T-squared (tsq) 19.7614
F statistic (fstat) 4.6607
Numerator degrees of freedom (df1) 4
Denominator degrees of freedom (df2) 50
p-value (p_val) 0.002824

Simultaneous confidence intervals

compute_CI_diff = function(a, x_1bar, x_2bar, S, p, n_1, n_2, df1, df2) {
  critical_val = sqrt((p * (n_1 + n_2 - 2) / (n_1 + n_2 - p - 1)) * 
                  qf(0.95, df1, df2) * ((n_1 + n_2) / (n_1 * n_2)))
  margin = critical_val * sqrt(t(a) %*% S %*% a)
  c(t(a) %*% (x_1bar-x_2bar) - margin, t(a) %*% (x_1bar-x_2bar) + margin)
}

a_vectors_diff = diag(p)
CIs_diff = apply(a_vectors_diff, 2, compute_CI_diff,
                 x_1bar, x_2bar, S, p, n_1,
                 n_2, df1, df2)
